patch.objective: Network services: DHCP, SLAAC, DNS, NTP, PTP, and NTS

sources.cite: CompTIA Network+ N10-009 Exam Objectives, Version 4.0: Networking concepts 23%, Network implementation 20%, Network operations 19%, Network security 14%, Network troubleshooting 24%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16 of a copy of CompTIA's objectives PDF hosted by a training provider. Relevant text: 3.1 'Explain the purpose of organizational processes and procedures' (change management); 3.3 'Explain disaster recovery (DR) concepts' (RPO, RTO, cold, warm and hot sites); 3.4 'Given a scenario, implement IPv4 and IPv6 network services'; 4.2 'Summarize various types of attacks and their impact to the network' (ARP poisoning, ARP spoofing, on-path attack; rogue devices and services: DHCP). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

sources.cite: IETF RFC 2131, Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (1997)
sources.note: Relevant text (section 4.4.1): 'The client collects DHCPOFFER messages over a period of time, selects one DHCPOFFER message from the (possibly many) incoming DHCPOFFER messages (e.g., the first DHCPOFFER message or the DHCPOFFER message from the previously used server)'; section 3.1: 'The client may choose to wait for multiple responses.' Read in primary text on 2026-11-14. So a second DHCP server on the LAN wins some clients and not others.

sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, ipconfig (Windows commands), last updated 2023-02-03
sources.note: Relevant text: /all 'Displays the full TCP/IP configuration for all adapters'; /release 'Sends a DHCPRELEASE message to the DHCP server to release the current DHCP configuration'; /renew 'Renews DHCP configuration'. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14; the page lists no sample output, so the output layouts in the scenario are authored renderings in the Windows style.
